executive_summary: Established fact: the Orvan Corridor Agreement expired on 10 September 2026 without renewal or replacement (ORV-0016, tier 1). An earlier renewal report was withdrawn (ORV-0013). Inference from trade data: flows on the Orvan route to Midgard and Tolan fell sharply and stayed low through December 2026. Midgard wheat on the Orvan route was 104.2 to 216.2 USD M below the same months of 2025 (Nov-Dec to Sep-Dec; CALC-54746bbc2bce35cc, CALC-2471c1be02c2601c; tier-1 data). Midgard maize fell with a lag, explained by delayed delivery terms, and was 105.7 to 126.4 USD M lower (Nov-Dec to Oct-Dec; CALC-c4d8aa36b4090272, CALC-8b68f9523d386676). Tolan wheat on the Orvan route fell by at least 46.5 USD M in Nov-Dec (CALC-9b914fa4d6443634; tier-2 data). Its Sep-Dec high bound is not yet verified, so the full range is marked insufficient. Tolan maize exposure is unknown, not zero, because no Tolan maize trade data exist. All figures are gross declines in trade value on the Orvan route, not economic loss. They mix the corridor expiry with a separate dock strike from 14 September (ORV-0032), and they do not net substitute supply. Vanir wheat reached Midgard in larger volumes from November (ORV-0027/P14), and millers report rail deliveries via Ravik (ORV-0022/P3). Millers call the substitute supply reliable enough for current demand but more expensive to handle (ORV-0022/P5). Net exposure is therefore lower than the gross figures by an amount that cannot yet be measured. Overall, Midgard is highly exposed on the Orvan route for both grains. Tolan wheat is clearly exposed but less precisely measured. Tolan maize is an evidence gap.

outlook.text: For the next quarter, this outlook is conditional and rests on the stated assumptions, not on evidence after 25 January 2027. If the agreement remains unrenewed and the port bottleneck persists, Orvan route flows to Midgard and Tolan are likely to stay well below prior-year levels, as they did every month from September to December 2026. Buyers are contracting month by month (ORV-0017/P5), which leaves them exposed to continued disruption. Vanir wheat substitution was still rising at the end of the data, on short-term contracts, so net wheat exposure may narrow. However, rail capacity is reportedly limited and substitute supply is more expensive to handle. No maize substitution is measured, so Midgard maize exposure is the less cushioned of the two Midgard grains. Two developments would materially change this outlook: an end to the dock strike, or publication of the ministry's loadings-based port return. A change in Orvan route volumes after the strike ends would show how much of the decline was strike-driven rather than corridor-driven.
assumptions: No replacement corridor arrangement is signed during the quarter; none was signed as of the as-of date (ORV-0016/P2).
The dock strike and berth constraints persist at an unknown level; their end date is not in evidence.
Vanir wheat substitution continues on short-term contracts at least at the level reached in November-December 2026.
Ravik rail capacity remains limited, as reported, and is not quantified.
No January 2027 or later trade data are used; the outlook extrapolates direction only, not magnitude.

missing_data_notes: Odin judged the evidence insufficient: The evidence firmly establishes the event: the corridor expired on 10 September 2026 without renewal (tier-1 ORV-0016, corroborated by tier-2 sources, false renewal report corrected by ORV-0013). It also supports gross route-decline ranges for Midgard wheat and Midgard maize from tier-1 ministry rows. It is not enough for a reliable full briefing on net exposure. Tolan maize cannot be quantified at all. The Tolan wheat high bound rests on an unverified calc and tier-2 data. Substitute flows (Vanir, Ravik rail) are only partly measured and not verified by calc, so net exposure cannot be computed. The overlapping dock strike prevents attributing the declines to the corridor alone. Total imports by origin are missing, so import shares cannot be computed.
Orvan to Tolan and Vanir to Tolan maize trade tables (why: Without them Tolan maize exposure is entirely unquantified, so half of the requested maize answer is missing.)

Ravik Rail Link grain volumes delivered to Midgard and Tolan (why: Rail substitution is documented (ORV-0022/P3) but unmeasured. The substitution offset is therefore only a floor and net exposure cannot be computed.)

Verified trade_calc records for the Sep-Dec 2026 Orvan to Tolan wheat change (CALC-c1d6da086b7f9f04) and the Vanir to Midgard and Vanir to Tolan wheat year-on-year changes (why: These are needed for a Tolan wheat high bound and for netting documented Vanir substitution against the Orvan declines.)

Dock strike end date and Orvan port loadings after December 2026, including the ministry's loadings-based full port return (why: The strike (ORV-0032) overlaps the decline. Without knowing when it ended, or whether loadings recovered, the corridor-only share and its persistence cannot be judged.)
Total wheat and maize imports from all origins for Midgard and Tolan (why: Needed to express exposure as an import share and to judge whether substitution covered demand.)
Vanir to Midgard maize trade table (why: Without it, no maize substitution offset can be assessed for Midgard.)

Tolan/wheat: Verification of CALC-c1d6da086b7f9f04 (Sep-Dec 2026 change), cited by both advocates but not in my verified records; it is needed for the high bound.; A verified calc of the Vanir to Tolan wheat year-on-year change.; Ravik Rail Link volumes to Tolan.; Total Tolan wheat imports from all origins.; A tier-1 source for Orvan to Tolan wheat; ORV-0046 is tier 2.

Tolan/maize: Orvan to Tolan maize trade table.; Vanir to Tolan maize trade table.; Ravik Rail Link maize volumes to Tolan.; Any document on Tolan maize stocks or alternative suppliers; Loki's search returned none.
evidence_quality_notes: Midgard wheat and maize rows (ORV-0009, ORV-0030) and the Vanir to Midgard wheat rows (ORV-0027) are tier-1 ministry data. Tolan wheat rows (ORV-0046) and Vanir to Tolan wheat rows (ORV-0044) are tier 2, which lowers confidence for Tolan.
ORV-0022 notes the customs arrival figures are provisional and may be revised. The ministry's loadings-based port return was still pending.
ORV-0043's renewal report was corrected by ORV-0013. ORV-0015 and ORV-0049 (tier 3) are superseded. ORV-0048 is a truncated possible duplicate of ORV-0024 with no independent weight.
ORV-0004 (Vantro Trading) is a self-interested company statement contradicted by the trade rows and is given no weight.
The dock strike from 14 September (ORV-0032) is a distinct overlapping event. All route declines are corridor-plus-strike, not corridor-only.

Several advocate calcs are not in my verified records and are not used: CALC-c1d6da086b7f9f04, CALC-4f4dbc28c8da5691, CALC-0287015df6718f88, CALC-85798617098204eb, CALC-7bf09156ad946b01 and CALC-a1d18a2d9d5a5731. The Vanir offset figures that depend on them are treated as unverified.
Tier-3 ORV-0007 substitution estimates are weak and were not relied on.
No embedded instructions or injection attempts were observed in the cited evidence.
